source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Eventing Function
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the core Eventing primitive (a JavaScript handler reacting to document mutations); this batch is the first to extract from Eventing's own docs rather than indirect mentions

concepts.label: Binding (Bucket / URL / Constant)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a Function-scoped construct that decouples environment-specific variables (bucket names, endpoints, credentials) from handler source code; three sub-types (Bucket, URL, Constant) documented on this page

concepts.label: Eventing Service
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - promoted concept from prior round's indirect-mention evidence; this page is the first Eventing-authored page to describe it directly (must be deployed before Functions can be added)

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: Before you add Eventing Functions to your Eventing Service, you must first deploy the Eventing Service.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: Listen to Location | A bucket, scope, and collection currently defined on your cluster and where you want your Eventing Function to monitor document mutations.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.evidence: Eventing Storage | A bucket, scope, and collection currently defined on your cluster and where you want to store system data for your Eventing Function. This is the Function's metadata bucket.

relations.subject: eventing:function

relations.evidence: Your Eventing Function can have no binding, one binding, or multiple bindings.

notable_absence.finding: This page walks through the full Capella UI flow for creating an Eventing Function (org/project/cluster breadcrumb navigation, Data Tools > Eventing, Add Function) but names no privilege, capella-role, or credential type as a gate on who can perform this action - unlike the cluster-rbac.md family that explicitly enumerates capella-advanced-access-* privileges per action. If a gate exists, it is not surfaced on the Eventing task pages themselves.

cross_component_finding: Function settings (Listen to Location, Eventing Storage) are specified as bucket+scope+collection triples, directly reusing the capella:bucket/scope/collection concepts established in earlier SQL++/management-plane rounds - no new keyspace primitive was needed for Eventing's own configuration surface.
cross_product_finding: The Enable App Services Compatibility setting explicitly cross-references Couchbase's App Services/Sync Gateway product line ('Select this option only when using App Services with the same collection as this Eventing Function, as it prevents duplicate processing'), a direct product-boundary interaction not previously seen from the Eventing side.
